## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Lakkhaṇahāravibhaṅga* ("Conveying Characteristics: Analysis") is a section of the *Nettippakaraṇa* in the late canonical or paracanonical Pali literature. It presents the detailed analysis (*vibhaṅga*) of the *lakkhaṇahāra*, one of the sixteen interpretive modes (*hāra*) formulated in the treatise for the exegesis of canonical discourses [Law 1923]. Bimala Charan Law notes that the historical foundation of the *Lakkhaṇahāra* in the *Nettippakaraṇa* can be traced to the venerable Mahākoṭṭhita's explanation regarding how wisdom (*paññā*) and discriminative consciousness (*viññāṇa*) are inseparably conjoined in reality (*ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā no visaṃsaṭṭhā*), an epistemological principle also reflected in the *Milindapañha* and the commentaries of Buddhaghosa [Law 1923].
